rationale: The player is an appositional personal participant, immediately explained by the finite relative 'who covers his eyes'; it is not an action nominal.

data.turoyo: U ḥa, d ḥzele qamoyo, hawo edi gəmṭaməṣ ʕayne.
data.translation: Dann hält sich der, den er zuerst gesehen hat, die Augen zu.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; the first found player becomes the eye-coverer.

data.turoyo: W iḏa d l oṯe mine ḥozalle, hiye gəmṭaməṣ disa ʕayne.
data.translation: Wenn es ihm nichtgelingt, sie zu finden, so hält er sich wieder die Augen zu.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; failed search triggers repeated covering, independently of the 94/417 quotation.

data.turoyo: Bəṯr ḥa mənne, yaʕni m am mahəzmone, gəmṭaməṣ ʕayne tawo, d qasəmwa, w ḥa ḥreno ste gtole i šutke b naqwo mede aw b kiste d ḥa mənne.
data.translation: Dann hält einer von den fliehenden dem, der richtig geraten hat, die Augen zu, und ein anderer versteckt den Wollgurt in irgendeinem Loch oder in der Tasche eines Kameraden.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; another person's eyes are covered, demonstrating non-reflexive valency.

summary: All six tokens support the existing eye-covering sense. A possessive eye object can belong either to the actor or to another player (94/447); no new sense follows from that alternation.
The same 94/421 source contains agent mṭamṣono and finite komṭaməṣ. Reclassify the existing nominal example instead of claiming the agent form is missing.

The game rules contrast first-round covering, reassignment after someone is found, repeated covering after failure, and another player covering the guesser's eyes. These are discourse roles of one lexical action.

94/421 carries an explicit alignment warning: the supplied German adds striking and kissing one's hand, absent from the Turoyo verse. Neither flagged occurrence supplies a new quotation. Verify edition boundaries before quoting that translation.
Confirm whether the agent label mṭamṣono is productive Part act. or a lexical game-role noun; personal reference rules out its present Nomen actionis filing.
